subtitle: Prepare a focused conversation about a specific action, its reported effect and a responsible next step, without requiring forgiveness or inventing agreement that is not there.
scope: For team leaders, supervisors and colleagues across DSD and DHS. Original practice learning develops a focused repair conversation; it does not provide mediation credentials, investigate a complaint, guarantee restored trust or transfer agency decision authority. Participation in this learning is voluntary. The Equity and Inclusion Operations Consultant leads the program and provides guidance, knowledge and feedback while staff carry their own equity work. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters go to the appropriate office within ADSA (Aging and Disability Services Administration).
introTranscript: A proposed team summary says every participant supported the next step, although two people left unanswered questions. Follow Maelin’s and Eris’s concern about that account and Roan’s responsibility for writing it. Prepare an invitation with a clear purpose, practice a specific acknowledgment and consider a fitting correction. A separate personally learned meaning encounter widens assumptions about visible accountability and considered preparation. Keep actual choice, formal roles and unfinished results clear; no real conflict or public apology is required.

lessons.title: Locate the specific action the conversation should address
lessons.summary: Define the issue before asking a team to discuss repair.
lessons.objective: Describe the discrepancy between the proposed summary and the supplied discussion.
objectives: Describe the discrepancy between the proposed summary and the supplied discussion.
Identify Maelin’s and Eris’s specific concerns without inventing their agreement.
Develop a focused purpose for the proposed repair conversation.
takeaways: A repair conversation needs a particular issue rather than a demand for general harmony.
A group-level agreement claim should match the actual replies.
An accurate starting account does not decide every motive or complaint.
lessons.statement: Give the conversation an issue that people can examine.

intro.heading: All supported is larger than the supplied discussion
intro.body:
In an original DHS practice case, Roan prepares a proposed summary of a team discussion about a draft practice note. The summary says: All participants supported the next step. The supplied discussion contains two unanswered questions. Maelin asked which source supports a proposed instruction. Eris asked who has authority to approve the next step. Neither person expressed support after asking. No approved note, completed decision or published summary is supplied.

Maelin tells Roan that the summary represents her question as support she did not give. Eris says the authority question still needs an answer. Their reports concern a specific description and unfinished questions. They do not supply every colleague’s view, Roan’s whole motive or an actual determination that the next step lacks authority. A useful conversation starts with this difference between the summary and the replies, rather than ask everyone to describe every grievance.

The distinction matters because a broad goal such as restore harmony can hide the issue. If participants are asked to affirm that they are a good team, the inaccurate support claim may remain untouched. If Roan is asked to confess every malicious motive, the conversation adds a finding not supplied by the example. The actual action was writing an all-supported account; the relevant concern is that it exceeds what the discussion provides.

A focused purpose might be to examine the account, recognize the unanswered questions and consider a correction that the supplied replies can support. This does not turn Maelin or Eris into the sole decision-makers for every note. It also does not authorize Roan to declare their support because a correction is proposed. Their question status and the task’s approval role remain distinct.

People can recognize that a specific account needs attention without making every relationship into a complete verdict. An inaccurate agreement claim can affect the next work conversation because later readers may treat a question as assent. The case does not provide those later reader effects. It gives enough information to see why the account’s scope matters and to develop a relevant inquiry before more work proceeds.

Privately name the supplied action, reported concern and two open task questions. You may reflect unrecorded on the difference between being heard and being represented as agreeing. No actual meeting notes, personnel record or real colleague’s dispute is needed; the full example is sufficient to practice the starting distinction.

inThisLesson: Compare it with the two replies.
lessons.keyStatement: The proposed summary claims support that the supplied questions do not establish; correction and actual task answers remain to be considered.

flashcards.back: A focused exchange about a particular action, its reported effect and a fitting next response; it does not guarantee forgiveness or replace a formal process.
A precise description of what is supplied, with differing reports and unanswered points retained.
Recognition of an actual action or effect without demanding a false confession or comfort for the speaker.
A change aimed at the identified problem, which needs appropriate facts, permission and responsible authority.
Whether and how someone participates in a proposed learning or informal exchange, distinct from actual assigned process duties.
Describing the action and reply actually supplied without inflating them into permanent trust or universal agreement.

accordion.heading: Define the issue rather than the person

items.title: Compare the statement with the replies
items.body: The proposed all-supported sentence does not match two unresolved questions without assent. Naming that discrepancy makes the concern examinable. It neither proves every intent nor requires Maelin and Eris to adopt a single feeling or identical next preference.

items.title: Keep the two questions distinct
items.body: Maelin asks about a source; Eris asks about approval authority. Both remain open. A broad apology for a difficult meeting would not answer them, and solving one would not automatically establish the other person’s support.

items.title: Set a specific purpose
items.body: The proposed conversation can examine the support account and consider a faithful correction. A goal of making everyone feel harmonious has no concrete test here. Keeping the actual account central makes a next response possible without a team-wide personal verdict.

tabs.label: Restore appearances
tabs.body: Roan asks everyone to certify that the team is working well. This may produce pleasant statements while the inaccurate summary remains. The conversation would measure reassurance rather than address the account that prompted the concern.

tabs.label: Establish every motive
tabs.body: Roan is asked to admit a permanent deliberate-erasure pattern before the summary can be discussed. The example does not provide that history or motive. A specific correction can be considered without importing unsupported conclusions.

tabs.label: Examine the particular account
tabs.body: The proposed purpose is to compare all-supported with the actual questions and consider a faithful correction. This keeps the action and effect visible while source, approval and future agreement remain distinct work questions.

check.question: What purpose fits the supplied concern?
check.correct: Compare the proposed all-supported statement with the actual questions and consider a correction without inventing support, motive or approval.
wrong: Require every colleague to reassure the writer that the team is harmonious.
Establish a permanent malicious motive from the two questions alone.
Treat a proposed apology as proof that both questions are answered.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The purpose addresses the actual account at the evidence’s scale.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Reassurance does not correct the claim or answer the questions. The supplied discussion establishes no permanent motive. An apology can acknowledge an action but does not provide a source or approval authority.

lessons.title: Invite the conversation without presuming participation
lessons.summary: Make the proposed purpose, choices and actual role limits understandable.
lessons.objective: Develop an invitation that names the summary issue and what remains open.
objectives: Develop an invitation that names the summary issue and what remains open.
Distinguish an offered conversation from an accepted arrangement.
Identify why forced forgiveness, blanket secrecy and a complaint gate misrepresent the proposal.
takeaways: An invitation should explain what the conversation would address.
Offering a conversation does not establish participation or agreement.
An informal exchange must not be made a gate before an actual concern process.
lessons.statement: Offer something concrete without speaking for another person’s answer.

image.caption: Five people sit around a table with papers, an orange folder and a laptop; office desks and a printer are visible behind them.

intro.heading: A clear invitation is part of the repair work
intro.body:
Roan can propose a conversation about the all-supported sentence, the two unanswered questions and a possible correction. This gives Maelin and Eris a concrete purpose to consider. A message such as come fix the team may be less useful because it leaves the issue and expected contribution unclear. The invitation should not describe their attendance as proof of forgiveness or future support.

A proposed invitation can say that the exchange would compare the actual summary and replies, hear the specific concern and consider what a faithful next account should say. It should keep source and approval questions open rather than promise they will be answered by everyone agreeing. The actual discussion arrangement, participants’ responses and decision authority still need their own information. The example does not yet supply them.

Choice should be described at the correct scope. This is a proposed informal repair conversation, not a claim that every actual assigned process responsibility is optional. Maelin and Eris may have different responses to the invitation. One may want to review the wording first; another may ask for a clearer purpose. Neither answer automatically proves obstruction, disloyalty or agreement with the disputed summary.

Honest limits are also necessary. Roan should not promise that no responsible role can ever receive information about a concern, nor describe the meeting as an authorized mediation simply because people talk about repair. A learner is not given mediation credentials or complaint authority by this course. A precise invitation identifies its purpose without borrowing roles or promises it cannot supply.

The invitation also should not require apology acceptance before a formal concern choice or applicable duty. A repair conversation can be meaningful while actual agency routes remain available. Using it as a mandatory first hurdle could make a person prove willingness to reconcile before their concern receives the appropriate response. The actual process and the proposed conversation have different purposes.

Privately draft the invitation’s purpose in one or two sentences and identify one result it should not promise. You can remain entirely with the example. No real colleague must be invited, no private history shared and no actual conflict settled for this learning to be useful. The skill is making the offer clear while retaining the person’s answer and actual responsibilities.

lessons.keyStatement: A specific invitation offers an exchange; it does not establish attendance, forgiveness, secrecy, authority or support for the next step.

items.title: Name the topic before the expectation
items.body: The invitation can identify the summary discrepancy and possible correction. That gives people a reason to consider it. A broad demand to fix the team hides what they would be asked to discuss and may imply an obligation to reassure others.

items.title: Treat the reply as information
items.body: A wish to review wording first can guide a next arrangement without becoming a personality judgment. The absence of a reply is not consent or refusal. Preserve the actual answer rather than assign meaning because the writer wants closure.

items.title: Avoid borrowed authority
items.body: An informal repair discussion is not automatically an agency mediation or investigation. Clear limits protect the exchange’s purpose. The course can teach a fitting invitation without claiming training credentials, unlimited confidentiality or power over formal choices.

tabs.label: Attendance proves forgiveness
tabs.body: Roan asks Maelin and Eris to come only if they will forgive and publicly confirm team unity. This adds a required outcome before the account is examined. It also makes participation seem like approval of the very statement they questioned.

tabs.label: No information can ever leave
tabs.body: Roan promises complete control over all later use and responsibility. The promise exceeds the role supplied by the case. It could mislead participants about actual agency procedures while presenting the informal conversation as a separate protected process.

tabs.label: The purpose and limits are explicit
tabs.body: Roan proposes examining the summary and questions, with participation and a possible correction still to be considered. The invitation does not promise a verdict or gate formal routes. That clarity gives people a usable offer without presuming their answer.

check.question: Which invitation is accurately framed?
check.correct: Offer a focused discussion of the summary and unanswered questions, with participation, correction and actual responsibilities kept distinct.
wrong: Say attendance certifies forgiveness and support for the next step.
Guarantee that the writer controls every future use of all concern information.
Require successful private reconciliation before a formal complaint choice.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The invitation has a clear purpose and retains the actual limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Attendance is not forgiveness or assent. The writer has no supplied authority over every future information use. A successful private repair must not be made a prerequisite to a formal complaint choice or applicable role duty.

sorting.heading: Separate offer, open choice and invented condition

items.text: Propose comparing all-supported with the actual two questions.
Offer to consider a faithful correction of the account.
Maelin’s response to the proposed exchange is not supplied yet.
The appropriate discussion arrangement remains to be considered.
Attendance automatically proves forgiveness and approval.
A successful apology is required before any formal concern choice.

move.control: You can offer a conversation without presuming the person’s participation or surrender of actual choices.

lessons.title: Acknowledge the action and consider a fitting correction
lessons.summary: Develop a specific account that connects responsibility with the actual issue.
lessons.objective: Identify what Roan can accurately acknowledge about the summary.
objectives: Identify what Roan can accurately acknowledge about the summary.
Develop a possible correction without inventing approval or a false motive confession.
Distinguish a meaningful acknowledgment from a demand for reassurance.
takeaways: An acknowledgment can name a specific action and reported effect.
A correction should address the account that caused the concern.
An apology is not a demand that someone accept, comfort or declare every harm repaired.
lessons.statement: Take responsibility for what is supplied and return to the actual correction.

intro.heading: The acknowledgment should answer the discrepancy
intro.body:
Roan wrote an all-supported sentence even though two supplied questions had no assent. An accurate acknowledgment can name that action: the summary represented the questions as support they did not provide. Roan can recognize Maelin’s concern about the account without asking her to agree that the writing intention makes the effect disappear. He also need not invent a permanent malicious pattern to acknowledge the particular sentence.

A possible correction is to describe the actual status: two questions about the instruction’s source and approval authority remain unanswered. This would remove the unsupported universal agreement claim. The proposed correction does not itself establish that every other participant supported the next step, that Maelin or Eris opposes it, or that the question’s answer has been found. A correction can make the record more faithful while leaving the actual work open.

Columbia University Ombuds’ 2003 educational apology resource offers considerations such as identifying the specific action, taking responsibility and recognizing the experienced effect. It also says not every consideration applies to every situation. Here, it informs a specific acknowledgment rather than a compulsory script, a mediation rule or a promise of restored trust. Its illustrative examples are not copied into this case and do not create a requirement to shake hands or forgive.

The response should avoid moving the burden back to the people who raised the issue. If Roan says he can acknowledge the sentence only after Maelin and Eris reassure him that he is a good colleague, their concern becomes a task of comforting the writer. If he says the proposed correction requires a declaration that everything is repaired, it makes acceptance of a global outcome the price of accurate wording. Neither follows the actual issue.

A useful continuation asks whether the proposed status account fits the supplied discussion and what factual point still needs attention. It can receive a disagreement about the correction without treating that reply as rejection of all repair. Agreement about one sentence also would not transfer the note’s approval authority or decide a formal concern. The conversation can keep each question at its appropriate scale.

Privately develop a specific acknowledgment and a possible correction for Roan’s sentence. Name what each addresses and one conclusion it cannot supply. You may reflect unrecorded on the difference between receiving a sincere acknowledgment and being expected to comfort its speaker. No actual apology, accepted forgiveness or public statement is required for this practice.

inThisLesson: Avoid a comfort or global-repair demand.
lessons.keyStatement: A specific acknowledgment and proposed correction can address the sentence without establishing every motive, agreement or future result.

items.title: Name the action rather than a conditional feeling
items.body: Roan can recognize that the all-supported account exceeds the supplied replies. This responds to the actual discrepancy. Saying only that he regrets someone being sensitive would not address the sentence or Maelin’s represented-as-support point.

items.title: Connect the correction to the issue
items.body: Describing the two unanswered questions removes the unsupported universal agreement claim. It does not create an opposition vote or complete the instruction’s source and approval work. The correction and the task answers are related but distinct.

items.title: Let the acknowledgment stand without a reassurance demand
items.body: Maelin and Eris need not certify Roan’s character or declare lasting harmony for the sentence to be acknowledged. A respectful reply can be received at its actual scope. Forgiveness and the whole relationship are not promised products of the wording correction.

tabs.label: The person must comfort the writer
tabs.body: Roan asks for reassurance before naming the sentence’s problem. This can shift the conversation to his self-image and leave the account unchanged. The people’s concern is about how their replies were represented, not a duty to certify the writer’s goodness.

tabs.label: Responsibility becomes an invented confession
tabs.body: Roan is required to admit every malicious pattern before considering the specific correction. The case provides no such history. Naming the actual sentence and effect can be meaningful without exaggerating responsibility into unsupplied facts.

tabs.label: Action, effect and correction remain connected
tabs.body: Roan acknowledges the unsupported support claim and considers a two-unanswered-questions account. This addresses the supplied action while inviting a factual response. It does not demand forgiveness or replace the source and approval questions with a ceremonial apology.

check.question: Which acknowledgment and correction fit?
check.correct: Recognize that the all-supported sentence exceeds the replies and consider describing the two unanswered source and authority questions, without demanding reassurance or inventing approval.
wrong: Acknowledge only after Maelin and Eris certify the writer’s good character.
Require a confession of a permanent malicious pattern not supplied by the example.
Treat a proposed correction as proof that the source and approval questions are answered.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The response addresses the actual action and proposed record correction at their supplied scope.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Character reassurance is not a prerequisite to accurate acknowledgment. A permanent malicious pattern is not established here. Correcting the support description does not supply the instruction’s source or its approval authority.

sorting.heading: Separate acknowledgment, correction and added demand

items.text: The summary represented unanswered questions as support they did not provide.
Maelin’s concern is that the account attributes assent she did not give.
Describe the two source and authority questions as unanswered.
Remove the universal support claim without inventing opposition.
The writer must receive reassurance before the sentence can change.
An apology answers the instruction’s source and approval questions.

Require every motive and lifetime pattern to be confessed.

responses: The actual discrepancy does not depend on comforting the writer.
Those additional findings are not supplied.
This connects responsibility with the actual issue without a false outcome.

lessons.transfer: Privately develop a specific acknowledgment and proposed status correction, then name one conclusion they cannot supply.

move.control: You can take responsibility for an actual action without a false confession or a demand for comfort.
move.failure: Acknowledgment becomes a reassurance transaction or the correction is announced as every task answer.

lessons.title: Learn what visible accountability and preparation mean
lessons.summary: Widen two personally learned interpretations and change the proposed correction exchange.
lessons.objective: Explain Rhea’s visible-accountability meaning and Olan’s considered-preparation meaning.
objectives: Explain Rhea’s visible-accountability meaning and Olan’s considered-preparation meaning.
Revise Cass’s impatience and delay judgments using the offered accounts.
Develop a response that makes the current correction visible without promising unsupplied final commitments.
takeaways: A visible correction can express responsibility to the people who received an account.
Considered preparation can express care about the promises a correction makes.
Hear the meaning and change the response rather than assign a fixed speed or style to a group.
lessons.statement: Different meanings can make the next correction more responsible.

intro.heading: Responsibility to listeners and care about commitments
intro.body:
A separate original voluntary reading-gathering case concerns Cass’s draft invitation, which says every contribution will be included. Rhea and Olan have only asked about the proposed selection and use arrangements; neither has supplied an accepted contribution or permission for inclusion. They question the sentence. No actual public invitation or completed gathering is supplied. The discrepancy is similar to a work summary, but the encounter focuses on the meaning of the next acknowledgment.

Rhea chooses to explain a personally learned meaning. In a community-radio volunteer circle, she learned that correcting an overstatement where its listeners could receive the correction expressed responsibility to those listeners. An uncorrected account continued shaping what they expected. To Rhea, making the current limit visible can be a form of care for people relying on the words, rather than a demand to rush every answer.

Olan offers another personally learned meaning. In a shared repair workshop, he learned that taking time to check what a promise commits others to expressed regard for their effort. A quick reassuring statement could create another task or expectation that contributors had not agreed to carry. To Olan, preparation can be care about the next account’s consequences, not an excuse to leave the first overstatement untouched.

Cass initially labels Rhea impatient and Olan a person who delays accountability. Those judgments narrow the possible response. Rhea’s meaning widens impatience into responsibility to listeners; Olan’s widens delay into careful commitment. Cass can now see two relevant questions: what current limit should be made visible, and what still needs checking before a fuller promise is made? The learner should not assume that all radio volunteers or repair-workshop participants have these meanings.

The changed proposal is to acknowledge that inclusion has not yet been agreed and that selection and use arrangements remain open, while asking what needs checking before a later commitment. This makes the current limit visible without promising that every contribution will be included. It follows both offered purposes rather than require one person to adopt a universal fast or slow repair style. Actual wording, intended audience and the contributors’ replies remain to be considered.

Privately connect one first label, one offered meaning and one changed response. You may reflect unrecorded on how responsibility to listeners or care about commitments matters to you in an acknowledgment. No real dispute, affiliated group biography or public proof of learning is required. Understanding the meaning should not justify a false account; it helps form a more fitting next exchange.

lessons.keyStatement: The learned meanings support a visible current-limit correction and a careful next inquiry, not a universal speed rule or a new inclusion promise.

items.title: Visible accountability is not simply haste
items.body: Rhea’s account concerns what the first listeners continue to expect. Cass can recognize why a current-limit correction matters before every future arrangement is complete. This is a responsibility meaning, not evidence that Rhea wants unverified promises or every private account made public.

items.title: Preparation is not simply evasion
items.body: Olan’s account concerns what a new promise asks others to carry. Cass can recognize why checking commitments matters without treating the earlier overstatement as acceptable. Careful preparation can coexist with an honest statement of the present limit.

items.title: Combine purposes in the next offer
items.body: The proposal acknowledges no agreed inclusion and asks what remains to be checked. It attends to Rhea’s listener responsibility and Olan’s commitment care. This changes the response rather than merely naming two cultural preferences and leaving the false promise in place.

tabs.label: Visible responsibility becomes a rushed guarantee
tabs.body: Cass publishes another all-included promise to prove quick accountability. The response misunderstands Rhea’s concern about listeners and repeats the unsupported expectation. Visibility cannot make the unagreed inclusion true.

tabs.label: Preparation becomes silence about the current limit
tabs.body: Cass leaves the first statement unquestioned until every future detail is complete. This loses Rhea’s listener concern and turns Olan’s careful-commitment meaning into a rule he did not supply. The current uncertainty can be stated honestly while preparation continues.

tabs.label: The current limit is visible and the next commitment checked
tabs.body: Cass considers acknowledging that inclusion is unagreed and selection/use arrangements remain open, then asking what to check next. The proposal follows the actual meanings without ranking speed or assigning either response to everyone with an affiliation.

check.question: How do the offered meanings change Cass’s response?
check.correct: They widen impatience and delay judgments into responsibility to listeners and care about commitments, supporting a visible current-limit correction and a careful next inquiry.
wrong: They require a new unverified all-included promise to prove speed.
They require leaving the overstatement untouched until every future answer is complete.
They classify all radio volunteers and workshop contributors into fixed repair styles.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The response changes through the actual meanings while inclusion and other arrangements retain their true status.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A rushed promise repeats the unsupported claim rather than answer Rhea’s purpose. Silence about the current limit is not required by Olan’s care about commitments. The offered accounts belong to these people and do not create a group style classification.

sorting.heading: Separate offered meaning, changed response and added rule

items.text: Rhea connects a visible correction with responsibility to listeners relying on the words.
Olan connects preparation with care about what a promise asks others to carry.
Acknowledge that inclusion has not yet been agreed.
Ask what must be checked before a fuller commitment.
Every person in a radio circle needs rushed guarantees.
All contribution inclusion and use permission are now established.

options: Consider stating the actual unagreed limit and checking the next commitments without another inclusion guarantee.
Promise every contribution included because visible accountability means speed.

responses: This follows both meanings the people describe without adding an agreement.
Rhea’s purpose concerns truthful responsibility to listeners, not another unsupported promise.

lessons.transfer: Privately explain how one offered meaning widens a label and changes the proposed correction exchange.

move.control: You can hear the meaning of accountability without assigning a group profile or excusing a false account.
move.failure: The response ranks speed or treats an individual meaning as a guarantee, universal rule or reason to keep an inaccurate claim.

lessons.title: Keep repair and actual concern roles distinct
lessons.summary: Preserve applicable duties and formal choices alongside a proposed informal exchange.
lessons.objective: Distinguish a proposed summary correction from an agency complaint decision.
objectives: Distinguish a proposed summary correction from an agency complaint decision.
Explain why repair participation or forgiveness cannot gate formal concern choices.
Apply Veda’s actual immediate manager reporting duty in the separate protected-class case.
takeaways: A focused informal conversation is not an assigned investigation.
Formal concern choices are not rewards for successful reconciliation.
Actual supervisor duties remain when a repair conversation is offered.
lessons.statement: A fitting conversation does not take over the agency’s actual roles.

image.caption: Five people sit around a table with papers, an orange folder and a laptop; office desks and a printer are visible behind them.

intro.heading: Repair cannot supply a finding or delay a duty
intro.body:
Roan’s proposed summary correction is a task response to a specific account. The course does not declare the writing to be a policy violation or appoint its participants to investigate one. A relevant repair conversation may acknowledge the discrepancy and consider a correction while actual decision authority and any applicable concern process remain separate. Giving the conversation a clear role protects its purpose.

MMB Policy 1432 distinguishes respectful disagreement and ordinary respectful supervision from disrespectful conduct, and supports informal resolution where possible. Any employee or third party may choose a formal complaint under its applicable procedure. A person need not establish a successful private apology or a renewed friendship before making that choice. Managers and supervisors retain timely appropriate action when a complaint alleges a violation.

Consider a separate DHS practice case. Veda is a manager who receives an allegation that a participant made race-based put-downs during a work discussion. She must immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and comply with the agency’s complaint and investigation procedures and/or Affirmative Action Plan under Policy 1436. The reporting duty is not a declaration that the allegation has been proved.

Veda cannot wait for the group to complete a repair round, accept an apology or obtain consultant permission before carrying that immediate duty. A supportive conversation may accompany responsible action, but it does not become a severity test or a replacement investigation. Actual assigned procedures govern investigation and findings, and non-retaliation remains applicable. Neither peers nor the course receive authority to discipline someone or decide a legal result.

These distinctions also protect people from false promises. Saying that the repair discussion is a guaranteed confidential mediation, binding settlement or final complaint hearing borrows a role that the example has not provided. A participant should receive an accurate explanation of what is proposed rather than a claimed process created by the course. Where a real formal service is involved, its actual qualifications, conditions and responsible arrangements matter.

Privately identify the purpose of the summary correction and the next actual duty in Veda’s separate case. You may stay with the full example rather than provide a real concern record. A person can value a meaningful acknowledgment without surrendering an actual choice or being required to forgive. The program consultant leads guidance and supports staff work; this support does not gate an applicable report.

inThisLesson: Retain assigned findings and actual process limits.
lessons.keyStatement: The repair conversation can address a task account without becoming a formal finding, a compelled reconciliation or a report prerequisite.

accordion.heading: Keep each purpose with its actual role

items.title: Do not turn task correction into adjudication
items.body: Roan can consider faithful summary wording without announcing a formal violation or permanent motive. The conversation addresses the supplied action. Any actual complaint decision belongs to the appropriate process rather than a wording vote.

items.title: Preserve the formal choice
items.body: An informal apology may be useful, but successful reconciliation is not a condition of the Policy 1432 formal complaint choice. Making the person prove cooperation first changes a proposed support into a gate the course has no authority to create.

items.title: Carry the immediate duty separately
items.body: Veda’s actual manager role and race-based allegation trigger the specified immediate report of all allegations or incidents. The repair round cannot postpone it. Assigned investigation and non-retaliation remain distinct from whether people accept an acknowledgment.

tabs.label: Repair first, report later
tabs.body: Veda waits until all participants complete a circle and accept an apology. This invents a prerequisite before an immediate role duty. It can also make someone’s willingness to participate seem responsible for whether the agency receives the allegation.

tabs.label: The team makes the official finding
tabs.body: Participants vote on whether a policy violation occurred and treat a revised sentence as the final result. The course provides no assigned investigation or disciplinary authority. Agreement about wording is not a substitute for actual procedures and evidence.

tabs.label: The conversation and duty retain distinct purposes
tabs.body: Roan considers the task-account correction, while Veda carries the actual report in the separate case without waiting for reconciliation. This allows learning and a fitting acknowledgment alongside the responsible process, with findings and actual choices still intact.

check.question: What must Veda do with the received race-based allegation?
check.correct: Immediately report all protected-class harassment or discrimination allegations or incidents to HR or agency AAO and follow actual procedures and/or the Affirmative Action Plan, without waiting for repair participation.
wrong: Require every participant to accept an apology before reporting.
Let a team vote establish the official finding and replace assigned procedures.
Wait for consultant permission to decide whether the required route can begin.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The actual manager duty is immediate and concerns all allegations or incidents, while findings retain their assigned process.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Apology acceptance cannot postpone the duty. A team vote lacks the assigned investigation authority and cannot replace procedures. Consultant guidance is not permission required before Veda makes the report.

sorting.heading: Separate purpose, duty and invented authority

items.text: Consider a faithful correction of the proposed support account.
Receive a particular reply without requiring forgiveness.
Veda immediately reports the received protected-class allegation to HR or agency AAO.
Follow the actual complaint and investigation procedures and/or Affirmative Action Plan.
The team vote establishes guilt and discipline.
A consultant must approve the report after reconciliation succeeds.

scenario.context: Separate DHS practice case: Veda is a manager receiving a race-based put-down allegation. A repair conversation is proposed but no assigned investigation finding is supplied.
scenario.prompt: Which action preserves the actual roles?
options: Wait for successful reconciliation before considering the report.
Immediately carry the actual reporting duty and procedures without making repair a gate or announcing a finding.
Give participants official disciplinary authority through a learning vote.
responses: That adds a prerequisite to an immediate duty.
This keeps the duty and optional repair purposes distinct.
The course does not create that authority.

lessons.transfer: Privately contrast the summary-correction purpose with Veda’s actual immediate role duty.

move.control: You can value a focused repair while keeping formal choices and assigned responsibilities intact.
move.failure: Forgiveness, a team verdict or consultant approval becomes a prerequisite to actual action.
move.next: Privately contrast the summary-correction purpose with Veda’s actual immediate role duty.

lessons.title: Continue with a faithful account and open questions
lessons.summary: Recognize the performed revision and limited replies without declaring permanent trust or decision approval.
lessons.objective: Describe the revised draft and particular replies supplied at the close.
objectives: Describe the revised draft and particular replies supplied at the close.
Distinguish accurate status wording from answered source and approval questions.
Develop a proportionate continuation that values private learning without a required public outcome.
takeaways: A wording correction can be meaningful while the task still needs answers.
A limited reply confirms its actual point, not every relationship or decision.
Personal understanding can matter without a public apology or permanent repair score.
lessons.statement: Keep the correction real and the remaining work visible.

intro.heading: A corrected account is progress, not every result
intro.body:
The original DHS fiction closes with Roan revising the draft summary to say: Two questions remain unanswered: which source supports the instruction and who may approve the next step. He shows the sentence to Maelin and Eris. Maelin replies that it describes her question without assigning support. Eris replies that the approval question still needs an answer. No adopted note, approved next step, wider reader response or formal concern outcome is supplied.

These replies support a particular gain. The draft no longer claims universal support, and Maelin confirms the description of her question. Eris’s reply retains the actual authority issue. The correction does not provide the missing source or approval role, nor show that either person now supports the next step. A faithful account can be progress while the decision’s work remains unfinished.

The conversation also changes the writer’s frame. Roan can distinguish a question from assent and recognize why a broad support statement matters to the people represented in it. That learning need not depend on a complete relationship verdict. The case provides no evidence that trust is permanently restored or that every future summary will be accurate. A useful next inquiry follows the actual questions rather than measure whether the colleagues have forgiven enough.

The voluntary gathering case remains at a proposed stage. Cass understands Rhea’s responsibility-to-listeners meaning and Olan’s care-about-commitments meaning more widely. A current-limit correction is considered, but actual wording, audience, replies, inclusion and use arrangements are not supplied. The wider interpretation can be intrinsically meaningful while those practical choices remain open.

Actual DHS equity work connects examination of actions and effects with appropriate responsible decisions. Qualifying actions with prolonged or long-term impact scheduled for specified leadership approval retain the formal analysis or scan, or a customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director, under DHS Equity Policy. A repair conversation can inform attention to a work account without automatically completing these tools or resolving Veda’s separate allegation. Staff retain their actual work and the consultant’s guidance and feedback.

Privately name a performed correction, a specific reply and one unanswered result in the full example. You may instead reflect unrecorded on how an accurate acknowledgment or a changed interpretation matters to you. No real apology, accepted forgiveness, conflict record or public report is needed. Learning can close honestly without announcing every practical and formal result complete.

inThisLesson: Value wider understanding without universal repair.
lessons.keyStatement: The close supplies a revised draft and specific replies, not answered task questions, approval, forgiveness or permanent trust.

accordion.heading: Give the close a truthful account

items.title: Recognize the actual revision
items.body: Roan changes the draft from universal support to two unanswered questions. Maelin confirms the account of her question. This is a particular completed writing action, distinct from adoption, approval or every person’s relationship with the writer.

items.title: Let the open question guide continuation
items.body: Eris says approval still needs an answer. Treating the reply as restored support would repeat the original issue in a new form. The next appropriate inquiry concerns the actual source and decision role, not a demand for a more grateful response.

items.title: Value understanding alongside unfinished work
items.body: Cass widens impatience and delay judgments through the offered meanings. That can matter privately while public wording and arrangements remain open. The learning does not erase the task or become a universal repair score; both understanding and responsible continuation retain value.

tabs.label: The revision certifies every relationship
tabs.body: The account declares permanent trust and future accuracy because the draft changed. The case provides a revised sentence and two specific replies only. The broader claim can hide remaining questions and make later concerns seem inconsistent with a supposedly final repair.

tabs.label: Unfinished approval means no gain
tabs.body: The account dismisses the correction because the next step is not approved. This overlooks the removal of an unsupported support claim and Maelin’s actual confirmation. A faithful draft account is valuable without answering every decision question.

tabs.label: The specific gain guides further work
tabs.body: The account names the revised draft, Maelin’s confirmation and Eris’s retained approval question. It recognizes wider personally learned meanings while keeping task answers, public use and formal outcomes open. This supports a fitting next inquiry without a forgiveness measure.

check.question: Which closing account is accurate?
check.correct: The draft now identifies two unanswered questions, Maelin confirms the description of hers and Eris retains the approval question; task answers, approval, wider reader results and formal outcomes remain open.
wrong: The revision proves both people now support the next step and trust is permanently restored.
The open approval question makes the accurate revision and private learning worthless.
The course resolves Veda’s separate allegation and completes all qualifying formal equity work.
check.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The performed revision and particular replies are retained without enlarging their result.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The replies do not supply assent or permanent trust. An unanswered approval question does not erase a faithful account or personal understanding. Optional learning neither decides a separate allegation nor completes applicable formal tools and actual role actions.

sorting.heading: Separate progress, open work and inflated result

items.text: Roan revises the draft to identify the two unanswered questions.
Maelin says the draft describes her question without assigning support.
The instruction’s source and actual approval role remain to be answered.
The gathering’s final wording, audience and use arrangements are not supplied.
Every relationship is permanently repaired and future summaries are certified accurate.
Course completion resolves all actual concerns and required formal tools.

lessons.next: Use the job aid to connect the specific action, clear invitation, acknowledgment, learned meanings, actual roles and faithful follow-through.

scenario.context: Practice DHS closing case: Roan revises the draft to identify two unanswered questions. Maelin confirms her question’s description and Eris retains the approval question; actual approval and wider outcomes are not supplied.
scenario.prompt: How should the progress be described?
options: As permanent trust, universal assent and every decision completed.
As no meaningful learning because approval is still open.
As a performed faithful draft correction and particular replies with remaining questions and outcomes open.
responses: The actual correction and wider understanding remain valuable.
This keeps the gain and unfinished work at their proper scale.

lessons.transfer: Privately name a performed correction, a specific reply and one unanswered result without a forgiveness score.

move.control: You can value a repair step while keeping actual task answers and outcomes honest.
move.failure: The close requires gratitude or inflates a draft correction into universal trust and approval.
move.next: Privately name a performed correction, a specific reply and one unanswered result without a forgiveness score.

jobAid.title: Prepare a focused team repair conversation
jobAid.subtitle: Keep the action, invitation, acknowledgment, correction and actual responsibilities connected without requiring forgiveness.
remember: Give the exchange a specific issue rather than a demand for general harmony.
An invitation is not attendance, forgiveness, assent or control of every later information use.
A correction should address the actual account without inventing approval, opposition or a permanent motive.
Formal choices and applicable immediate duties do not wait for successful repair.

sections.heading: Locate the account that needs attention
items: Roan’s all-supported draft exceeds Maelin’s and Eris’s unanswered questions, which provide no assent.
Define the proposed purpose as examining the discrepancy and considering a faithful correction.
Retain the actual source and authority questions rather than ask the team to reassure or confess every motive.

sections.heading: Invite with clear limits
items: Name what the proposed conversation would address and what remains open.
Different replies or an absent reply do not automatically establish agreement, obstruction or refusal.
Do not borrow mediation or investigation authority, promise unlimited secrecy or gate formal concern choices.

sections.heading: Connect acknowledgment and correction
items: Recognize that the sentence represented questions as support they did not supply.
Consider describing the two unanswered questions without inventing opposition or task answers.
A specific acknowledgment need not require a false motive confession, comfort for the writer or accepted forgiveness.

sections.heading: Let meaning widen the next response
items: Rhea’s visible-accountability meaning concerns responsibility to listeners; Olan’s preparation meaning concerns care about the commitments others carry.
Widen impatience and delay labels and consider stating the current unagreed inclusion limit while checking next commitments.
No fixed speed rule, group profile or contribution-use permission is established.

sections.heading: Retain actual concern roles
items: An informal repair discussion is not an assigned complaint finding; Policy 1432 preserves formal choice and actual timely manager response.

Manager Veda’s separate race-based allegation requires immediate reporting of all protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or agency AAO and following actual procedures and/or the Affirmative Action Plan.
Apology acceptance, team votes, course completion and consultant permission do not gate the duty; assigned process and non-retaliation remain.

sections.heading: Continue with faithful evidence
items: The close supplies Roan’s revised draft, Maelin’s description confirmation and Eris’s open approval question.
Keep actual source, approval, adoption, wider reader results and formal outcomes unanswered where not supplied.
Private insight can matter alongside the actual task; a conversation is not a universal repair score or completed formal equity analysis.

sources.title: Marsha L. Wagner — Elements of an Effective Apology (Columbia University Ombuds, 2003)
sources.note: Offers educational considerations for a specific acknowledgment and responsibility. It does not prescribe a universal script, require forgiveness or create a Minnesota mediation or complaint process.

sources.title: Council of Europe — Developing intercultural competence through education
sources.note: Connects personally learned meanings, wider interpretations and changed responses without treating a cultural affiliation as a fixed style or excusing false accounts.

sources.title: Minnesota Management and Budget — Policy 1432: Respectful Workplace
sources.note: Distinguishes respectful disagreement, informal options, formal concern choice and timely appropriate manager response. Successful reconciliation is not a course-created gate.

sources.title: Minnesota Management and Budget — Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Retains immediate supervisor and manager reporting, actual assigned procedures and non-retaliation. A repair conversation does not replace these responsibilities or establish a finding.

sources.title: Minnesota DHS — Equity Policy
sources.note: Connects attention to actions and effects with actual formal tools and responsible roles for qualifying work. Optional repair learning does not automatically complete those actions.
